imagePrompt: Create one landscape 1536 x 1024 production sprite atlas: exactly TWO columns and THREE rows, six wide cinematic full-scene panels in row-major order 0,1 / 2,3 / 4,5. Each cell fills approximately 768 x 341 pixels (last row 342), flush edge to edge, no gutters or borders. Every cell is a standalone wide composition, not a square image pasted on a wide matte. Painterly literary motion-comic art: watercolor pigment, restrained ink contours, colored-pencil texture, natural anatomy, coherent perspective, grounded feet, credible hands, soft practical light. Keep faces and essential hand/object contact comfortably inside the cell. Show seated bodies joined naturally to chair and table; include chair seats, knees, ankles and shoes when visible. No detached limbs, paper-doll joints, rigid mannequin poses, extra fingers or floating props. Keep cast, clothing, anatomy, furniture and setting consistent across relevant cells. These are fictional adaptation illustrations, not portraits or photographs of real source subjects. NO lettering, labels, logos, readable writing, panel numbers, captions, speech text or watermarks anywhere. Chapter: Grounded. Cast/design continuity: A fictional adult male spaceflight aspirant, close-cropped dark hair and dark blue work clothes, at a plain preparation-room table. One solid unbranded helmet reflects a simple blue-white curved Earth. Neutral room, large empty wall space, no mission logo, real-person likeness or assertion of an actual flight.. CELL 0: Wide quiet preparation room. The aspirant sits beside a helmet on a sturdy table, leaning forward slightly toward the blue-white curved Earth reflected in its visor. His hands rest naturally beside the object, feet grounded under the chair. The reflected dream is subtle and contained entirely in the visor. CELL 1: Same room and helmet. He extends one relaxed hand close to the helmet without grabbing it, eyes following the reflection. A slight shift of light curves across the visor. No spacecraft, launch, injury or imagined achievement is shown outside the reflective surface. CELL 2: Same table after an unseen statement. The aspirant pauses mid-reach and turns his eyes toward an offscreen speaker, expression listening and uncertain. The helmet remains solid on the tabletop, reflection now still. No injury mechanism, severity, bandage or medical diagnosis is invented. CELL 3: Wide composition leaves a broad quiet area of plain wall beside the aspirant and helmet. He sits upright with one palm loosely open in a small question, eyes toward the offscreen voice. Empty space is intentionally empty; no diagram, text or optimistic picture appears there. CELL 4: Same quiet arrangement. His open hand has settled to the table beside the helmet. Brow softens into uncertainty and shoulders lower slightly. The visor reflection stays motionless and the plain wall space stays blank, with no answering person or event invented. CELL 5: Wide final room. The aspirant’s hand rests quietly beside the helmet rather than gripping or throwing it. His gaze rests between the object and the empty space beyond it. Ordinary light and unresolved stillness; no launch, recovery montage, despair spectacle or inspirational conclusion. Editorial limit: This is a preliminary dramatic concept, not verified biography. Do not invent an injury mechanism, medical detail, recovery or outcome.
